slides.texte_overlay:
How to master the art of
talking to strangers
Start where waiting happens. Queues, waiting rooms, train platforms. People are bored and open to a chat. "Is it always this slow here?" is often all it takes to get talking.
Ask for a small recommendation. "Have you tried anything good on this menu?" Asking for advice is the most natural opener there is, because it makes the other person feel helpful.
Keep your body language open. Phone away, headphones off, a small smile. You look approachable, and you'll be surprised how often strangers start the conversation for you.
Give a specific compliment. "That's a great camera, do you shoot film?" Noticing something real shows genuine interest and gives the other person an easy topic to talk about.
Read the signals and respect them. Short answers and looking away mean they're busy. Smile, wish them a good day, and move on. Respecting that is part of the art.
Make it a habit, not a performance. One small chat with a stranger every day. After a month, talking to people you don't know stops feeling scary and starts feeling fun.
Before: nothing to say to people I didn't know. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and an endless supply of things to ask and share with strangers.
